comparison: Perfect agreement on study design and baseline characteristics (C1-C11). Both evaluations rate these claims as SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly praising the large sample size and OpenEval confirming appropriate randomization and statistical validation of baseline comparability.

Perfect agreement on calibration results (C18, C74-C76, C81-C83). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers praising 'well-calibrated curves' and OpenEval confirming Hosmer-Lemeshow tests show no significant deviation from perfect calibration.

Perfect agreement on decision curve analysis (C84-C89). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers praising clinical utility and easy implementation, while OpenEval confirms nomograms outperform individual predictors across threshold ranges.

Perfect agreement on comparative performance metrics (C19, C90-C95). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the statistical comparisons and OpenEval confirming IDI and NRI metrics demonstrate NomogramII's superiority for Grade II PH.

Perfect agreement on superiority of multivariable approach (C114). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers implicitly supporting through praise of comprehensive methodology and OpenEval explicitly confirming nomograms outperform individual factors.

Perfect agreement on study limitations (C115-C116). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly identifying lack of external validation and regional specificity as weaknesses, matching OpenEval's acknowledgment of these critical limitations.

Perfect agreement on web-based tool availability (C96). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers praising user-friendly implementation and OpenEval confirming the tool enhances clinical applicability.

Partial agreement on mechanistic interpretations (C110-C112). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to C111 being explicitly hypothetical and cross-sectional design limitations, while reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as part of robust methodology without noting the speculative nature of causal claims.

Strong agreement on NomogramI variable selection and performance (C12-C14, C44-C51). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers praised robust LASSO methodology and satisfactory AUC values; OpenEval confirms internal consistency of statistical results and appropriate model refinement.

Overlap on LASSO variable selection process (C41-C43). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers initially had concerns but accepted detailed explanations in revision; OpenEval confirms systematic selection process is internally consistent.

Strong agreement on NomogramII development for Grade II PH (C15-C17, C54-C63). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers praised strong AUC values and well-calibrated curves; OpenEval confirms parallel analysis methodology is consistent and biologically plausible.

Partial overlap on NomogramI performance metrics (C12-C14). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers praised satisfactory performance; OpenEval notes good generalizability but also identifies moderate AUC (~0.72) as indicating limited discriminative ability.

Partial overlap on NomogramI risk stratification (C64-C66). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers accepted risk stratification as part of clinical utility; OpenEval confirms high ORs support clinical utility despite moderate overall AUC.

Partial overlap on NomogramI superiority over individual factors (C70-C73). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers praised comparative superiority; OpenEval confirms nomograms outperform individual factors but notes moderate discriminative ability.

Partial overlap on NomogramII discrimination performance (C15-C17). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers praised strong AUC values; OpenEval confirms substantially better discrimination than NomogramI (0.84 vs 0.72) with acceptable generalizability.

Partial overlap on NomogramII risk stratification (C67-C69). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers accepted as part of satisfactory performance; OpenEval confirms higher ORs indicate stronger predictive capability for severe PH.

Partial overlap on NomogramII superiority over individual factors (C77-C80). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers praised satisfactory performance metrics; OpenEval confirms superior discrimination and stronger risk stratification for Grade II PH.

Significant disagreement on clinical utility claims (C117-C120). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims about effectiveness in remote areas require prospective external validation; reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, praising user-friendly implementation despite acknowledging ECG limitations.

Significant disagreement on future clinical application (C121-C122). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, stating claims extend beyond internal validation and require implementation studies; reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, confirming clinical significance and utility despite external validation limitations.

OpenEval evaluated study methodology and ethical procedures (C97-C107) as SUPPORTED but noted lack of information about exclusion criteria and selection bias. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these methodological details.

OpenEval evaluated statistical software specifications (C108-C109) as SUPPORTED but noted limitations in reproducibility details (missing R packages, random seeds, missing data handling). Peer reviewers did not specifically address statistical software documentation.

OpenEval evaluated background literature claims (C20-C40) as SUPPORTED, noting these are established medical knowledge with appropriate citations rather than original findings. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background/contextual claims.

OpenEval specifically identified C113 (mechanistic interpretation about AF and PH) as part of UNCERTAIN evaluation, noting it represents interpretation rather than study finding and causal direction cannot be established from cross-sectional design. Peer reviewers did not separately address this claim.
